title: The training intensity distribution among well-trained and elite endurance athletes
population: Retrospective and prospective TID studies in competitive endurance athletes across disciplines
findings: Most retrospective studies show a pyramidal TID with a high proportion of high-volume low-intensity training.
Some world-class athletes appear to adopt a polarized TID during certain phases of the season.

Authors state that emerging prospective RCTs showed superior responses of endurance-related variables with polarized TID in well-trained and recreational individuals versus high-volume or threshold emphasis (since moderated by the larger syntheses above).
limitations: Narrative review from 2015 that predates the 2019-2025 meta-analyses; abstract lacks quantitative pooled results.
implications: Supports pyramidal as the commonest observed pattern and polarized as a phase-specific variant, reinforcing the engine's phase-dependent TID design.
Do not cite its statement of polarized superiority; use the 2024-2025 syntheses instead.

verification.notes: Added by verifier. Crossref: Front Physiol 6, online 2015-10-27, two authors match. Statements taken from the abstract.
